gen-gf-gluten-fs-rowan: Rowan brings a friendly, literary serif body with generous curves and thin strokes about half the weight of its thick ones. And Gluten above it is plain and commanding, a display heading with lower contrast that would feel lost if shrunk too small.
gen-gf-goblin-one-fs-paquito:
Expressive and commanding, Goblin One pairs fat stems with hairline links.

Paquito answers as a confident, approachable classic serif with caps barely taller than its lowercase, and a heading made small would lose the chunky anchors that give it weight.
gen-gf-gochi-hand-archivo: Gochi Hand crowds its lowercase up toward the cap line, giving headings a hand-drawn, inviting feel. Archivo follows with outward-opening curves and a commanding x-height, so the sans keeps an editorial, approachable footing under the handwriting.
gen-gf-gochi-hand-fs-epilogue: Lowercase that crowds toward the cap line gives Gochi Hand its hand-drawn, friendly look. But Epilogue is the one that stays unclamped, a tall-bodied sans with stubby ascender tips and a wire-like monoline skeleton for steady reading.
gen-gf-gochi-hand-fs-public-sans: Public Sans has a hefty lowercase and broad open counters, a trustworthy sans under a handwritten heading. Public Sans would hold a longer stretch of text firmly, with Gochi Hand adding its inviting, hand-drawn crowding only at the top.
gen-gf-gochi-hand-fs-supreme: Gochi Hand's lowercase crowds up toward the cap line, hand-drawn and friendly. And Supreme lays a crisp, heavy-looking strip of plain sans beneath it, letters held open, so the loose heading gets a firm footing.
gen-gf-gochi-hand-general-sans: General Sans keeps a steady pen pressure from first letter to last, with an x-height that fills the line. And Gochi Hand above it supplies the hand-drawn, friendly crowding, so a longer read moves smoothly around each bend.
gen-gf-gochi-hand-manrope: Manrope leaves a bright open gap at every curved letter's mouth, with a minimal step from cap to lowercase and one pen width throughout. Gochi Hand adds the hand-drawn warmth.
gen-gf-gochi-hand-satoshi:
Hand-drawn lowercase crowds up toward the cap line in Gochi Hand.

Satoshi's soaring x-height and wide-open e, every stroke cut to one width, make the pairing feel approachable and uncluttered against that handwriting.
gen-gf-gochi-hand-switzer: Switzer brings Swiss, wire-like letterforms with a tall waist line and c tips that never creep toward touching. Make Gochi Hand small and its hand-drawn charm thins out.
